intended_object: The canonical isomorphism End_K(V) ⊗_K R ≅ End_R(R ⊗_K V) of additive groups, rewritten as a `MulEquiv` between `Multiplicative` types. The docstring ("additive group comparison") and its only use, as the components of `endVectorGroupIso` in `GrpCat`, show this.
explanation:
The body is just `(endVectorLinearEquiv K V R).toAddEquiv.toMultiplicative`. It takes the existing linear equivalence End_K(V) ⊗ R ≃ End_R(R ⊗ V) and moves it across `Multiplicative`. `endVectorLinearEquiv` itself is built from Mathlib's `IsBaseChange.end` composed with `TensorProduct.comm`.

The only reason this declaration exists is to turn an additive isomorphism into a group isomorphism in `GrpCat`. The library models additive group functors as `Multiplicative` groups, and `endVectorGroupIso` uses `(endVectorMulEquiv K V R).toGrpIso` for its components. So this is an encoding device and contributes no mathematical content of its own; the mathematical content is in `endVectorLinearEquiv` and `IsBaseChange.end`.

As an encoding it is correct. It is the canonical comparison map, it is basis-independent, and on pure tensors it sends f ⊗ r to (s ⊗ v ↦ rs ⊗ f v). The underlying isomorphism would hold for any finite free module over a commutative ring, which is the setting of `IsBaseChange.end`. The library, however, works throughout over a field K with V finite-dimensional, so a field is the natural setting here.
